ratification_queue.finding: WRONG TWICE, THEN SETTLED BY THE DIRECTOR. Draft 1 read 'both hands are BARE FLESH, no gauntlet anywhere' with forbidden:[gauntlet,glove] on both - which would have made the gate refuse the truth. He zoomed and asked whether that was not a gauntlet. Draft 2 then swung to 'the armour is ASYMMETRIC, one gauntlet not a pair'. Also wrong. HIS ACCOUNT, which is the canon: the same glove and brace are on BOTH arms; the front view shows the sword hand palm-on, which is why it registered as flesh. twin_back.png confirms the gold brace on both arms - and the advisor had that file the whole time and never opened it.
ratification_queue.drafted: N18 'brown leather gloves' on both hands, from his description. The forearm rows are back to N10 exactly as the record had them.
ratification_queue.needs: one naming ruling, not an observation. He calls the leather the GLOVE (hand, extending up under the brace) and the gold the ARM BRACE. The record's N10 is 'brown leather bracers' and N11 is 'a gold plate on each outer forearm'. If the leather is a glove that reaches the forearm, N10 may be naming the glove's upper half under a different word, and the hand and forearm rows may want one occupant between them rather than two.

ratification_queue.finding: THE _L/_R SUFFIX IS UNDEFINED IN THE SCHEMA. Nothing says whether L means the character's left or the viewer's left, and until this figure turned out to be asymmetric it did not matter - every paired surface carried the same occupant, so the convention could be wrong without any consequence. It matters now: one hand is armoured and one is not, and a prompt built from a mirrored table would put the gauntlet on the wrong arm.
ratification_queue.drafted: the two hand and forearm rows are named by what they DO ('sword hand', 'free hand') rather than by side, so the corrected reading cannot be mis-applied while the convention is open.
ratification_queue.needs: a convention ruling, after which the side suffixes can be trusted for every paired surface in this file and in longsword.surfaces.json.

ratification_queue.finding: THE GREAVE WAS NOT A HOLE, IT WAS A MIS-DECOMPOSITION. There is no bare shin between the gold knee plate and the boot: the plate is large and angular, covers knee through upper shin, and its lower point overlaps the boot shaft directly. Brown leather and grey fleece are visible behind and beside it.

The Director: there is a brace on BOTH arms. N11's 'each' is right and its placement is right. The claim was built on the same front-on projection error as Q1. AMENDMENT 15 IS UNDISTURBED and N11 remains its example; its dE 1.07 no-response goes back to the co-location explanation.

ratification_queue.needs: OPEN, and it is the one genuinely untried move left. N9 'green cloth panels in the kilt' is recorded as a blocked addition that dropped, and the panels are plainly in the reference. The co-location law says a spec cannot add to an occupied surface - so the open question is whether a surface showing two materials should carry ONE COMPOUND occupant, 'a dark red layered cloth kilt with green panels', instead of a base plus a blocked addition. Nobody has tested it and it would need a generation to settle.
